newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money rates stable on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: German call money rates stable on Tuesday.

text.p: German call money was characterised by stable rates on Tuesday, dealers said, with market-players keeping an eye on developments in the foreign exchange and futures market, dealers said.
Ample reserves saw call money trading in a narrow range around 3.05 percent, while one-year funds rose to 3.34/35 percent, compared to 3.30/31 percent on Monday afternoon.
"The Bundesbank doesn't really care about a five-basis-point rise in one-year funds," said one trader.
Effective central bank reserves on Monday were 41.6 billion marks, compared to 42.2 billion on Friday, the Bundesbank said.
Meanwhile the monthly average was 41.3 billion marks, compared to 41.2 billion on Sunday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average stood at 3.08225 (3.07483). The twelve-month FIBOR rose to 3.35000 percent from 3.26800 percent.
